This integration connects Gladys to **Sunricher DALI gateways** (SR-GW-EDA,
configured with the DALI Center app) **locally**, through the MQTT server
built into the gateway: no cloud, no other broker to install.

> **Never tested with a real gateway.** The protocol comes from the
> PySrDaliGateway library (Sunricher, Apache-2.0), used by Home Assistant.
> Unofficial, not affiliated with Sunricher.

## What the integration does

At every connection, and when you click "Scan" (once a minute at most), it
reads the list the gateway already keeps (it never starts a search on the
DALI bus):

- **DALI lights**: on/off, brightness, and by DALI type the colour temperature
  (DT8 Tc) or the colour (DT8 RGB, XY, RGBW, RGBWA).
- **DALI groups**: on/off and brightness of the group. The gateway gives no
  state of the group itself: Gladys shows "on" when a member is on, "off" when
  all are off (unknown while a member is unknown).
- **Scenes**: an "Activate the scene" button per scene of the gateway. Scenes
  are created and edited in DALI Center.
- **Motion sensors**: motion (instant) and occupancy (stays on until "vacant").
- **Light sensors**: lux (0 to 1000; a value outside is ignored).
- **DALI-2 push button panels**: no device, but a **scene trigger** "DALI
  push button panel" (panel, key number, event: pressed, held, double pressed,
  turned, released).

States come in real time (the gateway pushes them). Not supported yet: the
energy use of the lights, identify (blinking), sensor and driver settings.

## 1. Pairing: getting the credentials of the gateway

The gateway gives its MQTT **user name** and **password** only after its
button is pressed, as an answer to a request sent on the local network by UDP
multicast. The container of a Gladys integration does not see the multicast of
your network (Docker bridge): pairing is therefore done **once**, by a small
command on the Gladys machine (or any computer of the same network with
Node.js 22 or later):

```bash
docker run --rm -it --network host --log-driver none --read-only \
  --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges \
  ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-sunricher-dali:<version> node scripts/pair.mjs
```

(replace `<version>` with the installed version shown in Gladys; from a clone
of the repository: `node scripts/pair.mjs`).

`--network host` only serves to receive the multicast of your network; the
container is removed at the end (`--rm`). `--log-driver none` keeps Docker
from storing the output (so the password) in its logs; the other options take
from the container every right it does not need.

1. Run the command: it looks for gateways for 3 minutes.
2. Press the **Reset** button of the gateway **once, briefly**.
3. The command shows the **address**, the **MQTT port**, the **serial
   number**, the **user name**, the **password** and whether the gateway uses
   **TLS**.
4. Copy these values into the configuration of the integration, then clear
   the terminal: the password is shown there only (the command writes it to
   no file; with `--log-driver none`, Docker does not keep it either).

Options: `--serial <number>` (only that gateway), `--timeout <seconds>`. When
several gateways answer, the first one with credentials is shown: run again
with `--serial` for the others.

If the gateway answers by multicast, its answer (so its credentials, only
scrambled) can be read by any device of the network during the pairing: this
comes with the protocol of the gateway.

The request and the answer are scrambled with a fixed key published in
PySrDaliGateway: a convention of the gateway protocol, not a protection. The
`type: "HA"` field of the request is the one of the library Sunricher
publishes for Home Assistant; no other value is documented.

## 2. Configuration

- **Address of the gateway**: its IP address (give it a fixed address in your
  router).
- **MQTT port**: the one shown by the pairing (1883 by default).
- **Serial number**: as shown (on the SR-GW-EDA, the MAC address without
  separators; `A1:B2:…` is accepted, and 12 hexadecimal digits are put in
  capitals; another format is kept as typed, capitals included). It is part of the MQTT topics:
  the integration only takes the messages of **this** serial number, and
  ignores a message that names another one.
- **User name** and **password**: those of the pairing. The password is kept
  by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to the gateway,
  never written in the logs.
- **TLS**: only when the pairing says `TLS: yes`.
- **Certificate fingerprint** (TLS only, optional): empty, the first
  certificate seen must be signed by the Sunricher root authority (the one of
  PySrDaliGateway, shipped with the integration); it is then pinned and kept
  in `/data` **before** the password is sent. Typed, it is the one expected,
  signed by Sunricher or not.
- **Language of the names**: for the devices without a name in the gateway.

The **Test the connection** button tries a connection (when none is under way)
and shows what was read.

## Security and limits

- **Without TLS** (how the gateway works by default), the user name and the
  password travel **in clear** on your local network: the status of the
  integration says so. With TLS, a first certificate not signed by Sunricher
  is refused: **nothing is sent**, a stop with no new try, the status shows
  its fingerprint (enter it only if you are sure this is your gateway). If
  `/data` cannot keep the fingerprint, nothing is sent either. Then the
  certificate is pinned; if it changes, **nothing is sent**, the connection stops with no new try and the status
  shows both fingerprints. If you replaced or reset the gateway, enter the new
  fingerprint. Emptying the field never relearns a certificate.
- **Refused credentials** (answer 4 or 5 of the gateway, or two connections in
  a row closed or unanswered within 15 s after the credentials were sent): a
  stop kept in `/data`, **no new try**, even after a restart. It is lifted by
  changing the configuration (new credentials after a new pairing, typed while
  the integration was stopped included), or by "Test the connection" once a
  connection works. To see that the credentials changed, `/data` keeps 8 bits
  of a salted hash of the refused pair (never of an accepted one): useless to
  find it back; in 1 case out of 256, new credentials look the same and "Test
  the connection" is needed. A protocol error of the gateway is an ordinary
  cut (a spaced new try).
- **One MQTT session** at a time; reconnections spaced 10 s, 30 s, 1 min,
  2 min then 5 min; a container that restarts again and again connects at
  most once per 10 s (time of the attempt kept in `/data`).
- **Bounded messages**: 512 KB at most per message, bounded lists and names,
  1,000 messages per 10 s at most; a malformed message or one of another
  serial number is ignored.
- **Many lights**: commands of the same kind sent within 100 ms leave in a
  single MQTT message (32 devices per message); Gladys gets at most 240 states
  per minute, lights and motion sensors first; an unchanged value is sent
  again only every 30 minutes.

## Commands

A command is **acknowledged once written to the gateway**; the light (or the
members of the group, or the lights of the bus after a scene) is read back
1.5 s later and Gladys gets the real state. A command is **refused, nothing
sent**, exactly in these cases:

- the integration is not connected to the gateway, or the connection ended
  before the message was written;
- the command could not leave within 3.5 s;
- the device is not (or no longer) in the list read from the gateway, or
  belongs to another gateway;
- the value is not understood (on/off other than 0 or 1, brightness outside 0
  to 100, temperature outside 153 to 500 mired, colour outside 0 to 16777215,
  scene other than 1, empty value);
- the feature is read only (sensors).

A brightness above 0 also turns the light on; 0 turns it off.

## External ids

Frozen rule (it fixes the devices, their history and your scenes):
`light:<serial>-<bus>-<address>`, `motion:…`, `illuminance:…`,
`group:<serial>-<bus>-<group>`, `scene:<serial>-<bus>-<scene>`, with the serial
number in lower case, the DALI bus (channel) and the DALI short address.
Changing the DALI address of a driver creates a new device in Gladys.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Connected, but the gateway does not answer on the topics of this serial
  number"**: check the serial number (the one of the pairing).
- **Unreachable**: check the IP address and the port; a host firewall may
  block the traffic from the Docker bridge to the local network.
- **A light is missing**: it must be added to the gateway in DALI Center,
  then "Scan" in the Discovery tab.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Sunricher DALI asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your DALI gateway | `section` | No | For the Sunricher DALI gateways (SR-GW-EDA, DALI Center app). The integration talks to the gateway on your network through the gateway's own MQTT server: no cloud, no other broker. It reads the devices, groups and scenes configured on the gateway: DALI lights (on/off, brightness, colour temperature or colour), DALI groups, scenes (a button to recall each one), motion and light sensors; the keys of DALI-2 push button panels become scene triggers. The gateway gives its user name and password only at pairing: follow the guide (one command on a computer of your network, then the button of the gateway). One connection at a time. Never tested with a real gateway. Unofficial, not affiliated with Sunricher. |
| Address of the gateway | `string` | Yes | Its IP address on your network, as the pairing shows it; give it a fixed address in your router. |
| MQTT port of the gateway | `number` | No | As the pairing shows it (1883 unless told otherwise). |
| Serial number of the gateway | `string` | Yes | As the pairing shows it (on the SR-GW-EDA, its MAC address without separators; 12 hexadecimal digits are put in capitals). The integration only takes the messages of this gateway. |
| User name (from the pairing) | `string` | Yes |  |
| Password (from the pairing) | `secret` | Yes | Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to the gateway, never written in the logs. With TLS, sent only once the certificate of the gateway is checked (signed by Sunricher on the first connection, then the pinned one). |
| TLS (if the pairing says the gateway uses it) | `boolean` | No | Without TLS, the user name and the password travel in clear on your network (plain MQTT, as the gateway works by default). With TLS, the certificate of the gateway must be signed by Sunricher on the first connection, then it is pinned. |
| Certificate fingerprint (TLS only) | `string` | No | Optional: the SHA-256 fingerprint of the gateway certificate. Empty, the first certificate seen is kept if Sunricher signed it; enter a fingerprint to accept a certificate Sunricher did not sign. If the certificate changes later, nothing is sent and the status shows the new fingerprint: enter it here only if you replaced or reset the gateway. |
| Language of the names | `select` | No | Used for the names of the devices and features added from now on, when the gateway gives no name. |

## How to install Sunricher DALI in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Sunricher DALI appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-sunricher-dali:0.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-sunricher-dali](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-sunricher-dali).

Sunricher DALI requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Sunricher DALI is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
